features.title: Structure timer reminders
features.description: Mask admins can turn on Structure timers in Mask Admin > Discord to get a Discord reminder 24 hours, 1 hour and 15 minutes before a structure timer ends, and when it ends. In Tripwire you also get a pop-up and a sound at 15 minutes and at the end; turn that off in Settings > Kills & Intel > Timer alerts.

images.caption: The pop-up when a structure timer is close

features.title: Structure timers on the map and in one list
features.description: The Structures panel has a new clock button that lists every structure timer of your mask, soonest first, with Hostile only and Hide ended filters. Systems with structures or a timer in the next 48 hours get small icons on the chain map, the system info shows a one-line summary, and residents set by hand now appear first in the panel's residents strip. Turn the map icons off in Settings > Map Markers > Structure & timer icons; the panel itself is under Settings > Kills & Intel.

images.caption: The Timers view of the Structures panel

features.title: Nearest loot buyers
features.description: The Destinations window now lists the three nearest NPC stations that buy blue loot (Sleeper components), with security, station, gate jumps from your chain's exits and a Set route in game button. Tick Red loot to include the buyers of Triglavian Survey Databases. Turn it off in Settings > Routes & Navigation > Loot buyers.

images.caption: Nearest blue and red loot buyers in the Destinations window

features.title: Hide cosmic anomalies
features.description:
Pasting your scanner window used to fill the signature list with cosmic anomalies. Choose Show, Hide or Don't import under Settings > Signatures > "Anomalies in the signature list". Hidden anomalies stay in the list data and are folded away behind an "N anomalies hidden - show" line; Show is the default.

The wormhole dialog also now offers the Drifter holes (S877, B735, V928, C414, R259) when the destination is a Drifter system, and its Stable and EOL buttons explain the game's new "Reliable lifetime" and "Expired" wording.

images.caption: Anomalies folded away in the signature list

features.title: Threat: 90-day activity and busiest hours
features.description: The Threat & residents section in the Intel panel now shows a 7 day / 90 day profile of the system you are viewing: a small chart of kills by hour of day (EVE time), the busiest window (for example 18:00–22:00 EVE, also shown in your own clock), the top groups with kills on several different days, and how long ago it was analysed. Switch between 7d and 90d at the top of the block. History builds up from the first time a system is looked at, so a new system starts with a note about how many days it covers. Turn the whole block off in Settings > General Preferences > System threat & residents.

images.caption: Kills by hour and top groups over 90 days

features.title: Hole names for pasted holes
features.description:
When you open a pasted wormhole that has no name yet, the Edit Signature dialog now fills in the suggested name (A, AB, AB6 ...) just like adding a hole does. It is selected, so just type to replace it, for example when a K162 turns out to be a medium or small hole. The way-back side of an already named hole stays empty.

Don't want suggestions? Turn them off in Settings > Signatures > Suggest hole names.

images.caption: A pasted hole in a system reached through A gets the name AA

features.title: Mute button
features.description:
A new speaker button next to Settings in the top bar mutes all Tripwire sounds (kill sounds and voice, watchlist alerts) with one click, so you can work undisturbed. Click it again to unmute; it turns red while muted, and your sound settings stay as they are.

Don't want the button? Hide it in Settings > General > Mute button.

images.caption: The mute button (red: muted) next to Settings

features.title: Structures panel
features.description:
A new small Structures panel lists the structures in the system you are viewing (Upwell structures, POS towers, deployables), one line each with the type icon, owner ticker, state icon, timer countdown and how long ago it was seen. The strip at the top shows who lives here: one chip per owner (ours green, hostile orange, unresolved grey, with a structure count); click a chip to highlight their structures.

To record structures, paste a d-scan and tick Save structures to the system (or use Save structures only), or add one with the + button and set the owner, state, timer and note from the pencil on a row. Everyone on your mask sees the same structures, and they stay with the system when it leaves your chain. Turn the panel off in Settings > Kills & Intel > Structures panel.

images.caption: The Structures panel in a C5

features.title: Threat & residents in the Intel panel
features.description:
The threat level and the corporations active in a system now sit at the top of the Intel panel, in a "Threat & residents" section you can collapse (the threat level stays visible). Click "Set residents" to record which corporations or alliances live in a hole, with a short note; everyone on your mask sees them instead of the corporations guessed from kills.

If the Intel panel is turned off, the section stays in the system info panel. Turn it off entirely in Settings > Kills & Intel > System threat & residents.

images.caption: Residents set for a wormhole, in the Intel panel

features.title: Skyhook raids: lava or ice, and what they're worth
features.description: The Raidable skyhooks box now shows whether each planet is lava (Magmatic Gas) or ice (Superionic Ice), its number in the system, and a value rating from $ to $$$$$ (hover it for the estimated raidable ISK per hour). Ice hooks are always $, because lava hooks produce about 25 times more reagent; lava gets $$ to $$$$$ by how rich the planet is. Use the Planet checkboxes to show only lava or only ice, and sort by Value to put the richest raids first. Open the box from the skyhook icon on a low-sec or null-sec system.

images.caption: Lava and ice badges and raidable value in the skyhooks box

features.title: How to roll this hole
features.description:
The mass dialog now tells you how to roll a hole: a numbered list of passes for a battleship (or medium) roller crew, each marked safe, may collapse or will collapse, so nobody is sent out on a pass that could strand them. The ship buttons are coloured the same way, the jump log shows a running total and what is left, and the dialog refreshes itself while open.

Press Rolled (closed) when you are done and the Discord rolling message says who rolled it. Set your roller ships or turn the recommendation off in Settings > Wormhole Jumps & Mass > Roller ships.

images.caption: How to roll this hole in the mass dialog

features.title: Raidable skyhooks
features.description:
Low-sec and null-sec systems on the chain map now have a small skyhook icon next to the Jump planner ring (clicking such a system's name opens it too). It opens a box, "Raidable skyhooks near <system>", listing the skyhooks that can be raided now or soon within a number of gate jumps of that system: the system, region, jumps, and the raid window in EVE time with a countdown. The blue button sets the gate route in game. Close the box with its X and open it again from the icon.

In the box, choose how far away to look, low-sec and/or null-sec, whether to show only open windows or those opening within a few hours, and how to sort. Turn the icon off, or the opening on name click, or change the default distance in Settings > Routes & Navigation.

images.caption: The skyhook icon on a low-sec system and the Raidable skyhooks box

features.title: Routes avoid risky holes
features.description:
Routes through your chain (Favourites, Destinations and Fight here) now go round holes that are EOL, at critical mass, too small for your ship, marked preserve mass, or being rolled. If there is no other way, you still get the route with the fewest risky holes, with a one-line warning and an orange ring on those hops.

Tick One-way in the Favourites panel or Destinations window when you are not coming back, and EOL and critical holes are allowed again. Choose what routes avoid in Settings > Routes & Navigation > Routes avoid.

images.caption: No way round: the route with the fewest risky holes is used and they are flagged

features.title: Rolling: show which holes we are rolling
features.description:
Right-click a system on the chain map and choose Rolling… (or use the Mass dialog) to mark the hole you are rolling, with an optional note. Everyone on your mask sees an amber ↻ marker on the connection and "Being rolled by … since HH:MM EVE" in the mass dialog; choose Stop rolling when you're done. You can hide the markers in Settings > Map Markers.

Corp admins can post these marks to your hole-roll channel: Mask Admin > Discord > Rolling sends the hole's name, its system and the EVE time, and strikes the message through when rolling is done or the hole collapses.

images.caption: The ↻ rolling marker on a connection and the mass dialog line

features.title: Settings grouped into sections
features.description:
Settings are now grouped by what you are doing: Chain Map, Map Markers, Wormhole Jumps & Mass, Signatures, Routes & Navigation, Kills & Intel and General, plus the Jump Planner and Kill Reporting sections. Each section is short, and nothing was reset: your choices are kept.

Can't find something? Type in the new Find a setting box at the top of Settings to see only the matching settings.

images.caption: Settings in short sections, with the Find a setting box at the top

features.title: Who is in local: corporations, alliances and threat
features.description:
Open a shared local scan in the Intel panel to see its pilots grouped by alliance and corporation, with tickers, a zKillboard link and your own corp or alliance marked as friendly. Pilots in NPC corporations and unknown names are listed separately.

The panel also shows a zKillboard threat badge per pilot and group (danger %, a skull for dangerous pilots, solo hunters and cyno-capable ships). Lookups take a moment after a scan is shared. Turn either part off in Settings > General Preferences > D-scan & local intel.

images.caption: A local scan grouped by alliance and corporation, with threat badges

features.title: Discord: preserve mass marks
features.description:
Your corporation's Tripwire admins can now post preserve mass marks to Discord. When someone marks a connection "preserve mass", changes the reason or clears it, a message names the hole with its chain label, type and class, who marked it and why. Changes within 30 seconds edit the message, clearing the mark strikes it through without pinging anyone again, and holes that close are struck through automatically.

Set it up in Mask Admin > Discord > Preserve mass: pick a channel and who to ping, and choose whether only connections in your home chain are posted. It's off until an admin turns it on; there is no personal setting, because a preserve mass mark is a warning for the whole corporation.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord: the Preserve mass type and its preview

features.title: Watchlist pings only for your chain
features.description:
Watchlist matches are now posted to Discord only for systems connected to your home system (Mask Admin > Discord) through live wormholes, the same rule as "Any kill in our chain". Old chain fragments that are still on the map no longer ping, so admins will see fewer, more relevant messages.

Set a home system in Mask Admin > Discord; until one is set, no watchlist matches are posted and the page shows a warning. The pop-up, sound and highlight in Tripwire are unchanged. There is no new setting: the Watchlist match notification keeps its own on/off in Mask Admin > Discord.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord warns when Watchlist match is on without a home system

features.title: Jump planner: Get home
features.description:
The Jump planner has a new Get home mode. Pick the system your jump ship is in (type a name, or click Jita, Amarr or your last start) and it lists the low-sec and null-sec exits on the chain you can reach in one or two jumps, with how many wormholes lie between each exit and home. Click Dest to set your destination to the first cyno system.

It warns when a wormhole on the way home is too small for your ship, is EOL or is low on mass. Switch between From exit and Get home at the top of the Jump planner.

images.caption: Get home from Amamake: routes into the chain's exits, with the wormholes back home

features.title: Discord: notice when chain kills are paused
features.description:
If "Any kill in our chain" is on but the mask has no home system, Tripwire can't tell which chain is yours and posts no chain kills. Instead of going quiet, it now posts one notice to that Discord channel saying chain kills are paused and where to set the home (Mask Admin > Discord). Once a home is set, it posts one line saying chain kills resumed.

Nobody is pinged by these messages, and the Mask Admin > Discord warning shows when the notice was posted. There is no setting for it: set a home system or turn chain kills off and it stops.

images.caption: The paused and resumed notices in the chain kills channel

features.title: Smart notes: kill cards and link chips
features.description:
zKillboard kill links in system notes now show as a compact kill card: ship, pilot and corporation, system, ISK value, age (EVE time in the tooltip) and the number of attackers, with a red edge for your losses and a green edge for your kills. zKillboard, Dotlan and EveWho links become small chips, long links are shortened, and system names written in a note (like J163701) become chips you can click to view that system. Your notes are not changed; editing shows the plain links as before.

Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences > Smart notes.

images.caption: A kill card and link chips in a system note

features.title: Jump planner: find a system
features.description:
Type a system name in the new "Find system…" box in the Jump planner to see where it is in the list: its row is highlighted and scrolled to, and it is ringed on the mini-map. If it isn't listed, the box says why (high-sec, out of range, Pochven, cyno-jammed, …).

The planner's on/off switch is now also in Settings > General Preferences > Jump planner, and the gear in the panel opens its settings. Hide the search box in Settings > Jump Planner > System search.

images.caption: Finding O3Z5-G: its row and its spot on the mini-map

features.title: Fight here: pick the fleet comp
features.description:
The rally point is now Fight here. Right-click a system and pick one of your corporation's fleet comps from the Fight here menu: the banner, the system's colour on the chain map and the Discord message show the comp, and its Discord role gets pinged. Corporation admins set up the comps (name, colour, role, note) in Mask Admin > Fight here.

You can hide the fight banner in Settings > Chain Map Settings > Fight here.

images.caption: Fight here with a fleet comp: menu, banner and coloured route

features.title: Jump planner
features.description:
Low-sec and null-sec exits on the chain map now have a small blue range ring. Click it (or the exit's name) to open the Jump planner: pick your jump ship and Jump Drive Calibration and see every system you can reach in one jump, coloured by distance on a top-down map, with gate jumps and a Dest button to set your destination in game. It also shows whether you can jump to the exit from Jita or Amarr within two jumps, and lets anyone on the mask mark a system as cyno-jammed.

Turn it off or change the ship, targets and map in Settings > Jump Planner.

images.caption: The ring on an exit opens the Jump planner

features.title: Paste a d-scan anywhere
features.description:
Copy your d-scan results in EVE (click a result, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C) and press Ctrl+V anywhere in Tripwire: the d-scan box opens for the system you are viewing with the scan already filled in and summarised. Nothing is shared until you click Share.

Signature pastes work as before. Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences > D-scan & local intel.

images.caption: Ctrl+V of a d-scan opens the d-scan box with the scan filled in

features.title: Kill messages show the chain label
features.description:
Discord kill messages (kills in the chain, corp kills and corp losses) now name the system the way the chain map does, with the name of the hole leading into it, for example "AABCA · J105246". Systems without a name on your chain look as before.

To leave the label out, edit the message text in Mask Admin > Discord and use {system} instead of {labelSystem}.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord preview of a chain kill with its label

features.title: Discord chain kills: set your home system
features.description:
Discord "Any kill in our chain" notifications now only post kills in systems connected to your home system through live wormholes, re-checked every minute, so an old chain no longer pings after its connecting hole collapses or expires.

Admins: set the home system in Mask Admin > Discord. Until a home is set, no chain kills are posted and the page shows a warning. Chain kills can still be turned off on the same page.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord: the new Home system setting

features.title: D-scan and local scans on the map
features.description:
Paste a directional scan or the local member list into Tripwire and share a summary with your mask, pinned to the system. The new Intel panel follows the system you are viewing: click "Paste d-scan / local" at its top (or right-click a system on the chain map). Each scan shows as a chip (for example "D-scan 2 min ago · 14 ships · 1 HIC"); click it for ships by class, on grid and off grid, lit cynos and nearby structures. Systems with a fresh scan get a small dot on the chain map (cyan for d-scan, green for local). Move or resize the panel with Customize layout.

Turn it off, or change how long scans stay fresh and the on-grid range, in Settings > General Preferences > D-scan & local intel.

images.caption: The Intel panel next to the chain map, with a d-scan summary opened, and the dot on the system

features.title: Smaller return bookmark pop-up, only for the first pilot through
features.description:
The return bookmark pop-up after jumping out through a named hole is now a single small line at the top right, under the top bar, so it no longer covers the map. Click it to copy. The bookmark now starts with ! instead of <, for example !C (signatures already named <C still count).

It now only appears for the first pilot through. Once the far-side signature has an ID or name, or someone else has already jumped the hole, it stays quiet. To get it after every jump, or turn it off, use Settings > General Preferences > Return bookmark pop-up.

images.caption: The compact return bookmark pop-up, top right

features.title: Watchlist: get told when the chain has what you're looking for
features.description:
Your corporation's Tripwire admins can now set up a watchlist for the mask in Mask Admin > Watchlist: filters for a specific J-code or system, a region or constellation, a wormhole class, an effect such as Wolf-Rayet, a static (e.g. "has a C5 static"), a hole type such as H296 or a minimum hole size, and how many jumps it may be from you or from home. Everyone on the mask sees the filters in the Watchlist panel.

When something new on the chain map matches, you get a pop-up and a sound, the system gets an eye marker, the hole into it is highlighted, and its signature is marked in the signature table so you know which one to warp to. Admins can also have matches posted to Discord (Mask Admin > Discord > Watchlist match). Turn the sound, pop-ups, markers or the panel off in Settings > General Preferences > Watchlist.

images.caption: The Watchlist panel, matching systems and their highlighted holes on the chain map
Admins set the mask's filters in Mask Admin > Watchlist
Creating a filter

features.title: Favourites: route as jump markers
features.description:
Each favourite with a route now shows it as a strip of small markers, one per jump: squares are stargates, circles are wormholes, and hops into or out of Thera or Turnur are ringed circles (yellow for Thera, pink for Turnur). The colour shows the security or wormhole class of each system. Hover a marker to see the system, its region and how you get there; long routes are shortened to fit the panel.

Prefer the old "1g → 2wh → 6g" text? Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences > Show routes as jump markers.

images.caption: Routes in the Favourites panel as jump markers

features.title: High-sec region instead of hole type
features.description:
Holes into high-sec now show the system's region (for example "The Forge") on the chain map where the hole type used to be, so you can see at a glance where an exit lands. Hover the name to see the full region and the hole type.

Turn it off in Settings > Chain Map Settings > High-sec region.

images.caption: High-sec exits labelled with their region

features.title: Fitted jump mass
features.description:
When a tracked character jumps through a mapped wormhole, Tripwire logs the mass the jump really took, using your ship's current fitting from ESI (armor plates, prop module, Higgs anchor), and asks whether you jumped hot or cold. The mass dialog marks each jump as "fit" or "hull", and clicking the prop icon switches a jump between hot and cold. Rolling guidance uses these masses.

The fit lookup needs asset access, which your Tripwire admin turns on; then remove your tracking characters and add them again. Until then, jumps are logged with the hull mass and your hot/cold answer. ESI can show a refit up to an hour late. Turn it off, or turn off the hot/cold question, in Settings > Chain Map Settings > Jump mass.

images.caption: The jump log with fitted masses and the hot/cold question

features.title: Routes through Thera and Turnur
features.description:
Favourite routes and the Destinations window now also look at the public Thera and Turnur connections from EVE-Scout. When going through Thera or Turnur is shorter, the route uses it: every jump is a small marker, Thera hops are yellow circles and Turnur hops pink ones, and the signatures to warp to are listed next to the route (click one to copy it). Hover a Thera or Turnur marker for the hole type, the signature, the largest ship it takes and the life left. By default holes with under 4 hours left (EOL) are skipped.

Set route in game sends each gate stretch separately: the first one now, the next once you are out of Thera. Choose Thera, Turnur, your ship size and which holes to skip in Settings > General Preferences > Routes through; untick both Thera and Turnur to turn it off.

images.caption: Routes through Turnur and Thera as jump markers, with the signatures to warp to

features.title: Preserve mass on a connection
features.description:
Mark a wormhole as "preserve mass" so nobody rolls it or burns its mass, for example your home static or the hole a fleet needs to come back through. Right-click the system on the chain map and choose "Preserve mass…", or use the link in the Mass dialog, and add a reason if you like.

Everyone on your mask sees a violet ⊘ marker next to the connection's size tag (hover it to see who set it, when and why) and a "don't roll this hole" warning above the rolling guidance in the Mass dialog. Clear it from the same menu or the warning. The flag disappears when the wormhole is deleted. Hide the markers in Settings > Chain Map Settings > Preserve mass.

images.caption: The marker on the chain map and the warning in the Mass dialog
Right-click a system: Preserve mass…

features.title: Up-to-date ship and Pochven wormhole data
features.description:
Marauder and Black Ops battleship masses now match their lighter hulls from the September 22 patch, so the mass log and rolling calculator count them correctly.

Pochven wormholes now show a 12-hour life. The new Pochven-to-Pochven holes (I078, L687, O546) and the new holes into Pochven (O753, R327) now show their life and mass when you hover the wormhole type.

images.caption: Hovering a Pochven wormhole type shows its life and mass

features.title: Clearing the rally point strikes through its Discord message
features.description:
Clearing the rally point no longer posts a new message that pings everyone. The rally message itself is struck through and says who cleared it and when, shown in each reader's own time zone. When the rally moves after 30 seconds, a new message is posted and the old one is struck through with where it moved.

Corporation admins can change the cleared text in Mask Admin > Discord with the new {rally} and {time} placeholders. Masks still using the default texts get the new ones automatically.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord: the rally point preview, cleared and moved

features.title: Hole size on the connection
features.description:
The hole size tag (S, M, L, VL or XL: the largest ship that fits through) now sits on the line between two systems on the chain map, because it describes the wormhole, not the system. It works in every chain renderer and keeps its tooltip; a dimmed tag with a ? is still a guess from the system classes.

Turn the tags off in Settings > Chain Map Settings > Hole size tags.

images.caption: Size tags on the connections of the radial chain map

features.title: Rally point message shows the chain label
features.description:
The rally point message in Discord now names the system the way your chain map does, with the name of the hole leading into it, e.g. AABCA · J152820. When the rally is cleared, the message says which system it was on.

Corporation admins can use the new {label} and {labelSystem} placeholders in their own texts in Mask Admin > Discord. Masks still using the default texts get the new ones automatically.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord: the rally point preview with the chain label

features.title: Rally point channel in Mask Admin > Discord
features.description:
Corporation admins can now choose which Discord channel rally point changes go to: turn on Rally point in Mask Admin > Discord, pick the channel's webhook and, if you like, a role to ping and your own text for when the rally is set or cleared. Changes within half a minute still update the same message.

As before, you can keep your own rally changes off Discord with "Also post to Discord" in the chain map's right-click menu or in Settings > Chain Map Settings.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord: the Rally point notification with its channel and texts

features.title: Threat badges and system residents
features.description:
Each system on the chain map now shows a small badge with its kills in the last 7 days, coloured from grey (quiet) to red (busy), with a glow after a kill in the last hour. Hover it for the last hour, day, week, month and 90 days.

The system info panel shows the system's threat level and the corporations active there, with likely residents and lost structures marked. Turn the badges off in Settings > Chain Map Settings, and the info panel part in Settings > General Preferences.

images.caption: Threat badges on the chain map and residents in the system info panel

features.title: Rally point to Discord
features.description:
When you set, move or clear the rally point, Tripwire also posts it to your mask's Discord channel (the same one chain map pings go to), with the system, its class and region, who set it and a link back to the map. Several changes within half a minute update the same Discord message instead of posting new ones.

Untick "Also post to Discord" in the chain map's right-click menu to keep a rally change off Discord; Tripwire remembers your choice. You can also turn it off in Settings > Chain Map Settings.

images.caption: Right-click a system: Rally here, and Also post to Discord

features.title: Discord notifications
features.description: Corporation admins can have Tripwire post to Discord for the corp mask (and the corporation's custom masks) when a new wormhole opens a few safe jumps from a trade hub, and for kills in the chain and kills and losses of the corporation. Each notification can go to its own channel, ping a role or @here and use your own text. Set it up in Mask Admin > Discord with a webhook from your Discord channel (Integrations > Webhooks); nothing is posted until you do.

images.caption: Mask Admin > Discord on a Corp mask: webhooks and the notifications they receive

features.title: Signature age colouring
features.description:
Signatures nobody has updated for a while are now tinted in the signature table's Age column, so you can see at a glance what needs re-scanning: a light amber tint after 4.5 hours (12 hours for wormholes) and a stronger one after 24 hours. Hover the Age cell to see how long it has been. Editing a signature, or a paste that adds new info, resets it; wormholes already marked EOL keep their red countdown.

Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences > Colour signatures by age.

images.caption: Stale signature with its tooltip

features.title: Set route in game
features.description:
Send a route straight to your in-game autopilot. In the Favourites panel (for favourites with Route on) and in the Destinations window, click the blue autopilot button next to the route: Tripwire sets the gate part of the route it worked out as waypoints, so the autopilot flies exactly that route, including the safe, high-sec only one, instead of picking its own.

A small window asks which of your tracked characters get the route: tick them, or use Select all, then press Send (or Enter). Your tracked character is ticked the first time, and Tripwire remembers your choice after that. Characters whose EVE SSO login has expired are greyed out until you log in with them again.

Take the wormholes to the exit yourself; the autopilot takes it from there.

images.caption: The autopilot button in the Favourites panel and the Destinations window
Choose which tracked characters get the route

features.title: Worst-case rolling calculator
features.description:
The mass dialog (right-click a connection > Mass) now shows how much mass can be left in the hole in the worst case: nominal mass ±10%, minus the logged jumps, narrowed by the hole's stable, destab or crit state. Pick your ship, prop on or off for each pass, and Higgs, and it marks the out pass and the return pass as Safe, May collapse or Will collapse, and warns you when you could be stranded on the far side.

Turn it off in Settings > Chain Map Settings > Rolling guidance.

images.caption: Rolling guidance in the mass dialog

features.title: Chain kill feed
features.description:
A new Chain kills panel shows the recent kills in every wormhole, low-sec and null-sec system on your chain map in one feed, newest first, with the system and hole each kill happened in. When a system joins the chain its last hour of kills is loaded, and new kills appear as they happen; click a system name to view it, or a row to open the kill on zKillboard.

Move and resize it with Customize layout. Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences.

images.caption: The Chain kills panel with kills from several systems on the chain

features.title: System kill feed
features.description:
A new Kills panel shows the 20 latest kills in the system you are viewing: the victim's ship, pilot and corporation, the corporation that got the final blow, how many pilots were involved, when it happened and the value. Click a row to open the kill on zKillboard.

Like the other panels you can move and resize it with Customize layout. Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences.

images.caption: The Kills panel for the viewed system

features.title: Favourites panel
features.description: A new movable Favourites panel lists your favourite systems: add them with the search box, drag to reorder, and use the eye to choose which ones the chain map shows routes to. The route button highlights the way there from where you are, through the chain or by gates, as the shortest route or (click again) a safe route through high-sec only, with the jumps shown like 1g → 2wh → 6g. Don't want it? Turn it off in Settings > General Preferences.

images.caption: The Favourites panel with a shortest route (dashed) and a safe route (solid) on the chain map

features.title: Kill Reporting
features.description:
Tripwire now plays a sound and shows a pop-up when someone dies in a system on your chain map, with a link to the kill on zKillboard. There are four events, each with its own sound: a small gank, a large gank (more than 5 pilots), a kill by your corporation and a loss of your corporation.

Pick a sound for each event from the sound pack (robot voices, radio, alarms, tones or your browser's voice), set its volume and preview it with the play button in Settings > Kill Reporting. You can also turn the sounds or the pop-ups off there. Kills come from zKillboard and can arrive a minute or more after they happen.

images.caption: Pop-ups for kills in the chain
Settings > Kill Reporting: a sound and volume per event

features.title: Hole size tags on the chain map
features.description: Each wormhole on the chain map now has a small tag next to its type showing the biggest ship that fits through: S (frigates), M, L, VL (freighters) or XL (capitals, in orange). A dimmed tag with a ? (like XL?) means the wormhole type isn't known yet and the size is a guess from the system classes; hover a tag for details. Don't want them? Turn them off with "Hole size tags" in Settings > Chain Map Settings.

images.caption: Size tags on chain map nodes

features.title: Return bookmark after a jump
features.description:
When your tracked character jumps out through a named wormhole (for example AB), a panel appears at the top of the window with the return bookmark text, !AB (older versions used <, as in the picture). Click it (or press Enter) to copy it, then paste it into the bookmark for the wormhole you just came through.

The panel closes by itself after a minute, or with the small x.

images.caption: Return bookmark panel after a jump

features.title: Saved destinations
features.description:
Keep a list of k-space systems you often travel to, like Jita or your staging system, and see how many jumps each is from the nearest exit on your chain. Open it with the pin icon in the chain map toolbar or from Settings > Chain Map Settings > Destinations.

Tick Show (or Show all on map) to draw a destination on the chain map, attached to the exit it is closest to.

images.caption: The Destinations window
Destinations on the chain map

features.title: Automatic wormhole names
features.description:
When you add a wormhole signature, the Name is filled in for you using the chain naming scheme: A, B, C... from home, then the parent's name plus one more character further out (letters for large holes, 1-5 for frigate holes, 6-9 for medium holes). Type your own name to override it.

After you click Add or Save, the in-game bookmark text (for example =A C5 ABC EOL) is copied to your clipboard, ready to paste into a bookmark.

images.caption: Suggested name and copied bookmark

features.title: Rally point
features.description:
Right-click a system on the chain map and choose Rally here to make it the rally point for everyone on your mask. The system pulses green and the wormholes from where you are to it are highlighted, so you can see which holes to take.

The chain map header shows the rally system and how many jumps away it is; click the cross there, or choose Clear rally, to remove it.

images.caption: Rally point and route on the chain map

features.title: Statics in the signature Type quick picks
features.description: When you add or edit a wormhole signature, the buttons next to Type now show this system's statics, marked with a dot. Click one to fill in the type and its destination class in one go; once Leads To is set, the matching static is listed first.

images.caption: Static quick picks in the signature dialog

features.title: What's New
features.description: Tripwire now tells you about new features after they're added. This window opens once after each update; reopen it any time from Settings > General Preferences > What's new.

images.caption: Reopen from Settings
The What's New window
